title: Chapter 437
paragraphs: Chapter 437
125. The Attackers, The Brothers (5)
"Revenge. There was no grudge between you and me until today's events. So, the reason you attacked me is to achieve your revenge through the power of the Council of Elders."
As Jin responded, Lurtan's gaze turned to Talaris. It wasn't a glance to beg for life using an old friendship.
"Huh, why are you looking at me? Even without me, you wouldn't have been able to do anything to Tikan. Haven't you lost so much sense that you couldn't even calculate that much?"
Those who attacked Tikan were armed with the power to destroy a small country.
If Tikan didn't have Quicantel, it would have suffered significant damage or been completely wiped out.

"…I know. We didn't hear that Eunryong was here either. Like our swords have dulled, the Council of Elders seems to have become quite incompetent compared to my memory and recognition. This time, all the prior information was inconsistent, and there were many variables."
"Isn't it the role of Runcandel's executioners to perform their duties amidst such variables?"
"That's right, Talaris. But we are now exiles, not executioners. Anyway, it feels strange that you are acting on behalf of the 12th generation."
"Why is it strange? I'm just helping my son-in-law."
A creepy laugh seeped out from the twisted mouths of the exiles.
"I had a feeling that someday I would die so pathetically. I don't know if meeting an old friend at the end is a curse or a blessing."

"If you insist on choosing, it's closer to a blessing. Even when you were young, you sometimes had such sentimental talks for no reason. Lurtan, tell me how this happened. I haven't heard from you for a while, so I thought some of you had become Black Knights."
Talaris seemed curious about how they ended up like this. It was natural for them, who had built up a certain level of affection, even if they weren't close friends.
Jin also wondered why people of 'Executioner' level had been exiled.
Excluding the ten black helmets, the Executioner was generally the highest position that a Runcandel knight could reach.

'If they had committed treason, they wouldn't have just been exiled no matter how great their merits were. They would have been executed. But other than treason or betrayal, there is no reason for an Executioner to receive a punishment more severe than exile.'
He recalled the purges.
'I roughly understand.'
Jin and Lurtan's eyes met again.
Lurtan stared at Jin silently for quite a while. He had never thought that the 12th generation would decorate their end.
With a sigh and a chuckle, Lurtan opened his mouth.

"Twelfth generation, we have been knights of Runcandel and the swords of the family since before you were born. Although we couldn't wear black helmets, we were close to being the best among the Executioners at the time."
If Lurtan's face hadn't been crushed and he hadn't suffered terrible injuries all over his body, he could have become a Black Knight.
"When Sir Runcandel spent a long time in the Black Sea, we were transferred to the 1st generation as ordered by the family head."
"Luna's orders?"
It was the first time he heard that story. Luna, the only white whale in the world, was famous for her habit of not flocking, befitting her nickname White Whale.
"Everyone believed that the first generation would become the next family head. But then came the twelfth generation, around the time you were born."
It was declared that the first generation would not become the family head.
Luton continued speaking. Despite his face being all crumpled up, Jin could tell that he had a very bitter expression.
"From the family's guardian knights to executioners, from the family head's knights to the first generation's knights... our affiliation changed like this over the decades."
The next step should have been to become a knight of another generation or to join the Council of Elders and serve as a family executioner.
However, Luton and his team members faced an entirely unexpected future.
"Second generation..."
Joshua Runcandel. Luton mentioned the name and paused for a moment.
"We thought we would become his knights. Even before the first generation gave up the throne, Rosa often showed signs of wanting to support the second generation."
At that time, Chiron spent overwhelmingly more time in the Black Sea than in the Sword Garden.
That's why, as it is now, it was Rosa's responsibility to practically lead the family.
Rosa did not appoint the exiles as knights of the second generation.
At the time, there were fifteen members in Luton's team, which meant there were fifteen top-ranking executioners.
"As if we had no value, she just abandoned us."
As Jin had predicted when the conversation began, Rosa started to purge them.
As if trying to make Luton and his team members non-existent from the beginning, Rosa erased everything about them.
Their lives, families, acquaintances, animals they raised, and even people they knew.
Although Luton and his team members were formidable, being stabbed by a trusted sword was inevitable.
They never thought the family would abandon them.

"With the help of the Black Sword chairman, four out of fifteen managed to survive. We ended up like this, but one died not long after, and another died helping the Council of Elders a few years ago."
"So only the two of you remain?"
"Yes."
They had devoted their entire lives to the Runcandel family, but what was the reason for such cruel and miserable purging?
The expelled executioners could never be free from that question for the rest of their lives.
"It seems that mother thought you were too difficult for the second generation to handle."
"…Maybe. There would be no reason to purge us otherwise."

Luton and his team members were the ones who used to attack Talaris even without Chiron's orders when they were his knights. Talaris was so violent that it could be described as an 'aggressive beast.'
That's why Rosa did not make them knights of Joshua.
Also, the reason they were not assigned as family executioners within the Council of Elders was that the council was wary of gaining more power than necessary.
They were purged without even a chance to pledge their loyalty to other siblings who had not yet become generations or those who had just become generations.
Of course, it was an unacceptable reason for them.
However, they had no power to resist such unreasonable injustice. Their opponent was Rosa Runcandel.
"Hmm... Luton, there's one thing I'm curious about in that story."
Talaris narrowed his eyebrows and spoke.
"What was Chiron doing during all this? While Rosa was slaughtering you without any reason, was Chiron just standing by?"
Slowly, Luton nodded.
"Yes."
"Why?"
"...You're not really asking because you don't know, Talaris."
Talaris sighed.
It was because the image of a friend, whose emotions had become drier than a desert, came to mind.
"Even so, 30 years ago, Chiron cared about you quite a bit... So he really took no action even in that situation?"

"After the first generation gave up the throne, the family head acted as if everything in the world was disappointing for a while. Maybe because of that, we weren't even on his mind. You never cared about our news either, did you?"

"That's because I thought there would be no major problem with your safety. How could I know about the internal affairs of Runcandel? Chiron and I can't be compared when it comes to looking after you."
"That's true. There's no reason for you to know our news if the family head doesn't care. But aside from the family head, you were the closest to us."
Luton continued speaking as Talaris hesitated.
"Of course, it's not a story I brought up to blame you."
"Yeah, I know. You shouldn't blame me. If you had come to Hidden Palace to ask for help after surviving, that would be a different story."

"Right. We didn't go to you because we thought you had nothing to do with this. Although you were the closest to us because we lived without people around us, objectively it wasn't that special. To you, we were just past acquaintances."
Talaris shrugged his shoulders.
If you had come, I would have helped you somehow.
Talaris did not say those words out loud. There was no point.
There was a moment of silence.
"I have nothing more to say."
"It's up to me to decide that. I still have a few questions."
Jin said.
"You said earlier that the reason you hit me was revenge, is my mother the target?"
"Yes."
"Why is that?"
"The Black Sword Chairman must have given me orders for his own benefit. And everything he does is to become the family head."
"Do you really think that Jordan, the Elder Chairman, can defeat Joshua and become the family head?"
When Jin looked genuinely puzzled, Luton shook his head.
"It doesn't matter how likely it is. We have no other choice."
"In other words, you're going to realize your revenge through the Black Sword Chairman. But from what you're saying, it doesn't seem like he's helping you out of gratitude."
"Gratitude? We've paid back Jordan for using us like dogs whenever he wanted. If he hadn't created this mess and saved us, we might have been a little more grateful."
The expelled executioners were indeed driven by the desire for revenge.
"Alright, then let me ask you one last thing."
"What is it?"
"You said you survived with the help of the Black Sword Chairman, Jordan Runcandel. Does my mother know about this?"
"She doesn't."
"I see. If she knew, she wouldn't have let you live until now. And that fact is the only means for you to take realistic revenge against my mother... I'll offer you a more valuable death."
"... A valuable death?"
"You'll never see the future where the Black Sword Chairman becomes the family head. If you die by my hand as it is, it's just over, and your revenge can't be realized."
"What are you trying to say, 12th generation?"
As Luton raised his head, Jin continued.
"Go back to the Garden of Swords. Let them know that the Black Sword Chairman dared to defy my mother's modest orders. Damage my mother's authority. That's the most meaningful revenge you can take."
